content.text:
I submitted index 0 (Fe 0.84, Sb 0.16) as the best composition. Its EQE was 0.0178%, the highest of the three I measured, but that is still a very low absolute value.

| Index | Fe / Sb | EQE (%) |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | 0.84 / 0.16 | 0.0178 |
| 4 | 0.76 / 0.24 | 0.0032 |
| 13 | 0.52 / 0.48 | 0.0015 |

- **Index 13:** I measured this first because it is close to FeSbO₄. The MEGNet model predicts a band gap of about 2.08 eV for FeSbO₄, just below the 2.1 eV light, so it should absorb. It performed worst.
- **Index 0:** the Fe-rich end of the library. The MACE model puts hematite (Fe₂O₃) on the convex hull (0 eV/atom), meaning it is stable. This measurement was about 10 times better than index 13.
- **Index 4:** the Gaussian-process model suggested index 5 for the last measurement, and I chose its neighbour, index 4. I was testing whether a mix of hematite and FeSbO₄ in between would do better, but it came in about 5 times lower than index 0.

EQE fell as Sb increased across all three points, and the best result sits at the Fe-richest composition in the library. The true best composition is therefore probably at or near index 0, but indices 1–3 were never measured. I didn't use any of the XRD budget, so the phases present in these films are inferred from the models rather than confirmed.
